transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Um… mostly work. I’m a nurse, and on the floor I keep losing my train of thought. Like an IV pump beeps, or a call light goes off, or someone asks another nurse something, and then I suddenly can’t remember what patient flow issue I was in the middle of handling. It’s been… pretty hard to manage.
Did you have trouble staying focused as a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I did okay in school, but even in elementary school teachers would write that I was “bright but careless.” I was always losing worksheets or forgetting to turn in homework, and my mom had to sit with me most nights just to keep me on track.
Do you also have this same kind of losing-your-train-of-thought problem outside of work?

Yeah… I mean, it’s mostly bad at work. That’s the main place I notice it, because on the floor there’s always something interrupting me—an IV pump, a call light, someone talking nearby—and then I just… lose whatever I was in the middle of thinking about.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to deal with?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I mean, I worry when there’s something going on, but I’m not sure it’s like… constant worry for no reason.
Do you often misplace things you need, like your keys, phone, or paperwork?
I’m not sure… I mean, I misplace things sometimes, like anyone, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s a big pattern.
Outside of work, do these attention problems cause trouble in your daily life?

Yeah… some. I forget things I really meant to do, like calling someone back or paying a bill. Even appointments sometimes, or I’ll set a reminder and still somehow not follow through. It’s frustrating.
Did these attention problems get noticeably worse after a specific stressful event or major life change?
It wasn’t one specific event, exactly. It got a lot more noticeable after I took on expanded charge-nurse responsibilities… almost two years ago now.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?
Not really sure. I mean… I can sit still when I need to. I haven’t really thought of restlessness as a big thing for me.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
I don’t know… not really depressed, I guess. I’ve been stressed and worn out, but I wouldn’t say “down” exactly.
At home, do you also get distracted and lose track of what you were doing?

Yeah… at home some, but it’s more obvious at work. On the floor I lose my train of thought constantly—like an IV pump beeps, a call light goes off, or someone asks another nurse something, and then I just… forget what patient flow issue I was in the middle of.
Have these attention problems caused serious problems in more than one part of your life, not just at work?

I mean… the main serious thing is work. It’s gotten to the point where I’m on formal supervision, and other nurses have to double-check parts of my charge nurse follow-through. That’s… hard to say. It makes me feel like I’m becoming a liability instead of someone people can rely on.
When you’re reading something at home, do you often realize you’ve drifted off and have to reread the same part?

Sometimes, yeah. It’s not the biggest thing, though. The main issue is more when I’m on the floor—like something beeps, or a call light goes off, or someone talks nearby, and I lose what I was doing completely.
When you’re away from work for several days, do these attention problems get a lot better?

A little, maybe. But the main place I notice it is still work. On the floor, if an IV pump beeps or a call light goes off, I can lose my train of thought and forget what patient flow thing I was handling.
Do you often have the same kind of trouble finishing routine tasks at home, like chores or paperwork?

Yeah… I do. I’ll mean to pay a bill or call someone back, and then it just doesn’t happen. Even with reminders sometimes, I’ll see it and still forget to actually do it. Same with appointments occasionally. It’s embarrassing.
When you were not at work, did you still have these same attention problems?

Yeah. It’s not only work. At home I’ll forget basic things I meant to do, like paying a bill or calling someone back. Sometimes I even set a reminder, and then… I still don’t follow through. I’ve missed appointments that way too.
Before you became a nurse, did you already have this same pattern of getting derailed by interruptions and then forgetting what you were doing?

Yeah… I think so. It’s just a lot more obvious now at work. Like on the floor, if an IV pump beeps or a call light goes off, I’ll lose what I was doing and forget the patient flow thing I was in the middle of.
Have these attention problems caused serious problems at home or in your personal life?

Yeah… it’s caused problems. I don’t really like talking about it, but at work it’s gotten serious enough that I’m on formal supervision. Other nurses have to double-check parts of my charge-nurse follow-through now, and… it makes me feel like I’m becoming a liability instead of a leader.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks and keeping track of multiple steps?

Yeah. Especially when I’m charge nurse. I’ll have little scraps of paper, sticky notes, half-started lists all over the place, but I still can’t really sort out what needs to happen first. I end up just reacting to whatever is loudest, and then I’m rushing to catch up at the end of the shift.
When you’re doing something in a quiet setting with no interruptions, do you still have trouble staying focused?
I’m not really sure. I mean… quiet helps some, I think, but I haven’t paid close attention to it that way. It’s harder for me to say.
As a child, did your attention problems ever get you into trouble at school, like missed assignments or teacher complaints?

Yeah… I think so. Even in elementary school, teachers would write things like I was bright but careless. I was always losing worksheets or forgetting to turn in homework, and my mom had to sit with me most nights just to keep me on track.
